look_here_first: An ANNUAL milkvetch with showy bicolored purple-blue and white pea flowers, short appressed hairs and slender curved/flattened pods, not a thick inflated groundplum fruit. Check the banner/wing/keel color pattern, leaflets and fruit cross-section.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Fabaceae/Astragalus: alternate pinnate leaves, papilionoid pea flowers, and legumes; fruit shape, inflation, hairiness, and curvature are especially useful for species ID.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: annual with decumbent-to-ascending stems often under ~35 cm

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fine appressed (strigose) leaf and stem hairs; avoid confusing this with densely silver-scaled leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: several conspicuous purple-blue/white pea-type flowers clustered in short racemes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flattened curved-oblong pods generally ~17–27 mm long, NOT plump hairy balloon pods

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: separate from A. plattensis (large fleshy pubescent pod) and A. crassicarpus var. berlandieri (fleshy groundplum) by fruit form

lookalikes.differences: Previously marked perennial with inflated hairy pods in the provisional dataset; corrected against published Texas flora / Barneby: this is an annual with a flattened, curved-oblong pod. A. nuttallianus group shares smaller pea flowers and slim pods, so flower size and mature fruit shape both matter.
